title: Two polynomial terms on the blowup of a Cartier flag
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime and $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$. Let $Z\xrightarrow{a}Y\xrightarrow{j}X$ be closed immersions of Noetherian schemes with $\ell$ invertible. Assume $Y$ is an effective Cartier divisor of $X$ [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], $a$ is locally cut out by a regular sequence of length $m\geq1$, and $ja$ by one of length $m+1$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Write $E=C_{Z/Y}$, $F=C_{Z/X}$ and $K=C_{Y/X}|_Z$ for the conormal bundles. Use the ordinary etale supported classes and Chern polynomials of [lem-per-generalized-blowup-class], and abbreviate $A_a=A_{a,E}$ and $A_j=A_{j,C_{Y/X}}$. Put $\pi:B=\operatorname{Bl}_Z(X)\to X$ [def-nagata-global-blowup], $P=\mathbf P_Z(F)$, and let $G_P:H^q(P,\Lambda(t))\to H_P^{q+2}(B,\Lambda(t+1))$ be the operator from the canonically trivialized exceptional ideal $\mathcal O_B(1)$ in that construction. There is an exact sequence of vector bundles
$$0\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow F\longrightarrow E\longrightarrow0.$$
The strict transform $\widetilde Y=\operatorname{Bl}_Z(Y)$ is an effective Cartier divisor of $B$, and the Cartier ideal of $Y$ pulls back to the tensor product of the exceptional ideal and the ideal of $\widetilde Y$, compatibly with trivializations off $\pi^{-1}(Y)$. Set $\xi=c_1(\mathcal O_P(1))$, $k=c_1(K)$, and pull all $c_i(E)$ and $k$ from $Z$ to $P$. For the supported Yoneda product $A_a\cdot A_j$ on $X$, the two divisor terms in this factorization give the explicit identity
$$\pi^*(A_a\cdot A_j)=G_P\left((-1)^{m+1}c_m(E)+(k-\xi)\sum_{s=0}^{m-1}(-1)^sc_s(E)\xi^{m-1-s}\right).$$
The first summand comes from the restriction $A_a|_Z=(-1)^mc_m(E)$; the second from the Gysin operator of $\mathbf P_Z(E)\hookrightarrow\mathbf P_Z(F)$, whose ideal is $K\otimes\mathcal O_P(-1)$. In this diagram the successive Cartier Gysin operators commute, so both terms have the displayed common outer operator $G_P$. Finally the ordinary Chern coefficients obey
$$c_s(F)=c_s(E)+k c_{s-1}(E)\quad(0\leq s\leq m+1),$$
with $c_0(E)=1$ and $c_s(E)=0$ for $s<0$ or $s>m$. No smoothness or regularity of the ambient schemes is assumed.

source.place: Expose XVI, proof of Theorem 2.3.2 after Lemma 2.3.3, pp. 236-237: blowup along Z when j has codimension one, factorization of the Cartier ideal, alpha and beta, commutation of the two Cartier Gysin operators, and the displayed formulas for tilde-alpha and tilde-beta. Whitney relation: XVI Theorem 1.3. This is the blowup computation before the final polynomial identity, not Theorem 2.3.2 as a black box.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-regular-flag-blowup-geometry] to the flag with outer codimension one. It gives the exact sequence $0\to K\to F\to E\to0$ with ranks $1,m+1,m$, the exceptional Cartier divisor $P$, the strict-transform Cartier divisor $T=\widetilde Y$, and $P'=P\cap T=\mathbf P_Z(E)$. It also gives transversality, $\mathcal I_P=\mathcal O_B(1)$, the factorization $\pi^*\mathcal I_Y=\mathcal I_P\otimes\mathcal I_T$ with its specified trivializations, and $\mathcal I_{P'/P}=p^*K\otimes\mathcal O_P(-1)$, where $p:P\to Z$. All schemes used below are Noetherian: over a Noetherian affine chart the blowup has finitely many charts $R[J/f_i]\subset R_{f_i}$, each generated by the finitely many fractions $f_j/f_i$, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. The same argument applies to $T$, and projective bundles have finite polynomial affine covers. The prime $\ell$ remains invertible under every structural map.

source.place: XVI, proof of Theorem 2.3.2, p. 236 (diagram and ideal factorization); Noetherian chart check: Stacks Tag 00FN, algebra.tex, lemma-Noetherian-permanence

proof.text: For each regular immersion in question, the canonical symmetric-to-associated-graded map is an isomorphism: locally it is precisely the polynomial map on regular-sequence generators of [lem-pur-regular-sequence-graded-polynomial], and these canonical maps agree on overlaps. Thus the modified blowups in [lem-per-generalized-blowup-class] with the actual conormal presentations are the ordinary blowups $B$ and $T$. Put $S_E(\xi)=\sum_{s=0}^{m-1}(-1)^sc_s(E)\xi^{m-1-s}$, so the defining polynomial is $Q_E=-S_E$. On $P'$ its variable is the restriction of $\xi$, since both tautological quotients are induced by $F\twoheadrightarrow E$. For $b:T\to Y$, the defining characterization gives $b^*A_a=G_{P'\subset T}(Q_E|_{P'})$. Independently, the restriction clause gives $A_a|_Z=(-1)^mc_m(E)$. These use the construction and restriction formulas, without assuming compatibility of regular-immersion classes with composition.

source.place: XVI, Definitions 2.2.2.5 and 2.2.2.7, Lemmas 2.2.2.4 and 2.2.2.6; p. 236, formula for beta; associated graded identification: Stacks Tag 00LN, algebra.tex, lemma-regular-quasi-regular (1)

proof.text: Check the rank-one sign directly. If $I=\mathcal I_Y$, locally $I=(f)$ with $f$ a nonzerodivisor. Its Rees algebra is $R[ft]\cong R[t]$, whose Proj is $\operatorname{Spec}R$; the degree-one invertible sheaf identifies with $I$ and has the given frame off $Y$. These local identifications agree because they identify the same ideal and frame. In the rank-one construction of [lem-per-generalized-blowup-class], $Q=-c_0=-1$. Consequently $A_j=-e_Y(I,1)$, where $e$ denotes the supported Kummer boundary. This fixes the minus sign before expanding the divisor factorization.

source.place: XVI, Definition 2.2.2.7 in rank one; proof of Theorem 2.3.2, p. 236 (minus signs in alpha and beta)

proof.text:
Use the nested supported products and pullback of pairs of [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus]. The factorization from Step 1 and additivity for trivialized lines give $\pi^*e_Y(I,1)=e_P(\mathcal I_P,1)+e_T(\mathcal I_T,1)$, with supports enlarged to $\pi^{-1}Y$. Multiply by the pulled-back class of $a$ and use Step 3. The projection formula restricts that class to each divisor. On $P$ its restriction is $p^*(A_a|_Z)$; on $T$ it is $b^*A_a=G_{P'\subset T}(Q_E|_{P'})$ by Step 2 and pullback naturality in [lem-per-generalized-blowup-class]. Thus, in cohomology supported at $P$,
$$\pi^*(A_a\cdot A_j)=\alpha+\beta,\qquad \alpha=-G_P(p^*(A_a|_Z)),\qquad \beta=-G_{T\subset B}G_{P'\subset T}(Q_E|_{P'}).$$
The inner class on $T$ is supported at $P'$, so the second composite has support $P'\subset P$; the displayed equality uses its canonical enlargement to $P$. This is bilinear expansion of the Cartier class, rather than an invocation of the composition theorem being proved by this calculation.

source.place: XVI, proof of Theorem 2.3.2, p. 236, decomposition into alpha and beta

proof.text: The divisors $P,T$ are transverse by Step 1. Apply exactly the ideal-normalized Cartier-interchange identity in [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus] to them. It gives $G_{T\subset B}G_{P'\subset T}=G_PG_{P'\subset P}$, including their common support and Tate twists. Therefore $\beta=G_P(-\operatorname{forg}_{P'/P}G_{P'\subset P}(Q_E|_{P'}))$, where $\operatorname{forg}_{P'/P}$ forgets the support inside $P$. The forgetting is necessary because the input of $G_P$ is ordinary cohomology on $P$. Meanwhile Step 2 gives $\alpha=G_P((-1)^{m+1}c_m(E))$.

source.place: XVI, proof of Theorem 2.3.2, pp. 236-237, transverse Cartier interchange and formulas for tilde-alpha and tilde-beta

proof.text: Apply the forget-support formula of [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus] on $P$ to the class $Q_E$ and the ideal line $L=\mathcal I_{P'/P}$. It gives $\operatorname{forg}_{P'/P}G_{P'\subset P}(Q_E|_{P'})=Q_E\,c_1(L)$. By Step 1, $L=p^*K\otimes\mathcal O_P(-1)$. Kummer tensor additivity and dualization in that same cited node, followed by forgetting supports, give $c_1(L)=p^*c_1(K)-\xi=k-\xi$; pullback compatibility of Chern classes is [lem-per-noetherian-etale-chern-identities]. Since $Q_E=-S_E$, Step 5 becomes $\beta=G_P((k-\xi)S_E)$. Add this to the expression for $\alpha$. Bilinearity of the supported action gives exactly the displayed identity of the item. Every polynomial inside $G_P$ has bidegree $(2m,m)$, so its image has bidegree $(2m+2,m+1)$ as required.

source.place: XVI, proof of Theorem 2.3.2, p. 237, calculation of tilde-beta; XVI 1.1 (line additivity) and Theorem 1.3 (pullback)

proof.text: Specialize [lem-per-noetherian-etale-chern-identities] to $n=1$, identifying $\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$ with $\mathbf F_\ell$. Apply its Whitney identity to the exact sequence of Step 1. Since $K$ has rank one, $c_t(K)=1+kt$, and hence $c_t(F)=(1+kt)c_t(E)$. The coefficient of $t^s$ is $c_s(F)=c_s(E)+kc_{s-1}(E)$. Its normalization gives $c_0(E)=1$ and $c_s(E)=0$ for $s>m$; setting negative indices equal to zero gives the asserted endpoint conventions, including $s=0$ and $s=m+1$. No regularity of the ambient schemes enters any cited result.

source.place: XVI, Theorem 1.3 and p. 237, final conormal Whitney calculation
